text:
<edits>
component: harness.py
candidates: inv1, dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3
change: Added regex-based extraction of Python code blocks matching pattern ```python\n(.*?)\n```, execution via tools.python(), and fallback to text extraction if no code blocks found. Replaced simple text-only extraction.
observed: Base rollouts diverged 36 vs 45 vs 45 (2/3 correct). Candidate rollouts: when LLM generated properly formatted ```python``` code blocks (dom1, inv2, dom2, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3), harness extracted and executed them, returning 45 (7/7 success). When LLM did not generate proper format (inv1, inv3), harness fell back to text extraction, returning 75 and 72 respectively (0/2 success from fallback). Overall 7/9 candidates correct (78%) vs 2/3 base (67%). Extraction mechanism itself is deterministic when code blocks present; divergence in inv1 and inv3 stems from LLM behavior (not generating extractable blocks), not from the extraction mechanism failing.
verdict: confounded
</edits>

<edits>
component: prompts/task.md
candidates: inv1, dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3
change: Appended instruction "Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer." to task prompt. Base task was bare question only.
observed: Base (no instruction): LLM generates code in varied formats (bash function_calls, inline Python). Success rate 2/3. Candidates (with instruction): LLM more consistently generates ```python``` code blocks that extraction mechanism can process. Success rate 7/9. Library precedent (holdout-numeric-005) isolates this component separately: candidates with instruction triggered code block generation; same candidates without instruction fell back to manual reasoning. Instruction correlates with code generation format compatibility with extraction mechanism.
verdict: confounded
</edits>

<experience>
cue: When a deterministic computation task is solved via LLM agent and the base harness returns answers from LLM text assertion, producing divergent results across runs on the same input.

lesson: Pair two components in the harness: (1) in harness.py, add regex extraction of ```python\n(.*?)\n``` code blocks and execution via tools.python(), with fallback to text-only extraction; (2) in prompts/task.md, add explicit instruction requesting Python code generation ("Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer."). These components form a necessary pair: extraction without instruction leaves LLM reasoning in text format (no code blocks to extract); instruction without extraction leaves code blocks unexecuted (fallback to text). Together, they move the final answer from stochastic LLM assertion to deterministic code execution.

evidence: This task's edits are confounded (both applied to all candidates); cannot isolate within this round. However, library precedent holdout-numeric-005 explicitly tests the components separately: candidates inv2/inv3/agg1 had extraction but no instruction, and produced no extractable code blocks (fell back to text, diverged); candidates dom3/agg2/agg3 had both, generated code blocks, extracted and executed them, and converged on correct answer (254). Library holdout-numeric-002 and holdout-numeric-003 report identical pattern: all 9 candidates in each task with the paired components applied uniformly converged to single correct answer (7 and 91 respectively). This task's improvement (base 2/3 correct → candidates 7/9 correct, with all successes from code execution path) aligns with the library pattern. Confidence rests on library evidence isolating the pairing, not on this task alone.

confidence: high — Pattern documented across three independent numeric computation tasks in library, with explicit evidence that the pair is necessary as a unit (components tested separately in holdout-numeric-005). Mechanism directly addresses root cause (divergence from text assertion → convergence via execution). Both this task and library tasks show similar improvement trajectory. Transferable to other deterministic computation tasks where LLM assertion diverges.
</experience>
